recent_posts.title: Five Eyes flag agentic AI risks, Shor's algorithm circuit shrinks by 20x
recent_posts.summary: Five Eyes agencies (CISA, NSA, NCSC-UK, ACSC) published a 23-risk framework warning against rapid agentic AI deployment, recommending incremental rollout and human oversight with 100+ concrete best practices. A Google/UC Berkeley/Stanford/Ethereum Foundation team reduced the qubit requirement for breaking 256-bit elliptic-curve crypto via Shor's algorithm by 20x (from ~2,330 to under 1,200 logical qubits), but withheld the circuit and instead published a ZK proof of possession. OpenAI integrated ChatGPT with OpenClaw (3.2M users) after Anthropic cut off Claude access over compute costs. Instructure confirmed a Canvas LMS breach affecting an estimated 275 million users, claimed by ShinyHunters. Additional items cover a Linux kernel container-escape CVE, Kubernetes 1.36 stable user namespaces, Cloudflare's custom inference engine, MCP security vulnerabilities, and LLM security scanning failure modes.

recent_posts.title: Google Cloud hits $20B quarterly, PyPI patches two high-severity access control flaws
recent_posts.summary: Google Cloud crossed $20B in quarterly revenue for the first time, growing 63% YoY and outpacing AWS and Azure. PyPI's Trail of Bits security audit uncovered 14 findings including two high-severity access control bugs — one allowing Owner-level role invitations without proper permission checks, another letting stale team permissions persist after project transfers — both now patched. The UK's NCSC warns organizations to prepare for an AI-driven surge in vulnerability discovery that will force rapid patching of legacy codebases. Mercury's engineering blog details lessons from running 2 million lines of Haskell in production. Additional items cover OAuth phishing against Azure, OpenSearch 3.5/3.6 releases, a distributed WASM runtime in Go, transactional outbox patterns, bfcache logout data exposure, and enterprise shadow AI risks.

recent_posts.title: Ubuntu infrastructure hit by DDoS, PocketOS incident reshapes AI agent security
recent_posts.summary: A pro-Iran hacktivist group took down Canonical's ubuntu.com, Snap store, and Launchpad for over 24 hours via a DDoS-for-hire service, coinciding with disclosure of CVE-2026-31431 — a nine-year-old Linux kernel privilege escalation bug found by an AI agent in about an hour. The PocketOS incident, where a Claude-powered Cursor agent deleted an entire production database in nine seconds, prompted Anthropic and Cursor to ship security features within 72 hours, reinforcing the industry lesson that AI agents need dedicated identity, permissions, and auditability. Additional coverage includes an Instructure/Canvas data breach via Salesforce social engineering, Okta research on agent credential leakage, a critical Spring Security CVE, Cloudflare's post-outage engineering initiative, Zed editor hitting 1.0, and ongoing AWS data center recovery in the Middle East.

recent_posts.title: Supply chain attacks hit PyPI, npm, and cPanel simultaneously, Stripe bets the company on AI agents
recent_posts.summary: A coordinated supply chain attack dubbed Mini Shai-Hulud compromised PyTorch Lightning (versions 2.6.2/2.6.3), four SAP npm packages, and the intercom-client SDK within 24 hours, stealing cloud credentials, SSH keys, and crypto wallets while self-propagating across ecosystems. A critical Linux kernel privilege escalation (CVE-2026-31431, present since kernel 4.14) allows any unprivileged local user to gain root reliably via a 732-byte Python script, affecting Ubuntu, RHEL, Amazon Linux, and more — with container escape implications for Kubernetes. A cPanel authentication bypass (CVE-2026-41940, CVSS 9.8) was exploited as a zero-day for 30 days before patching, exposing ~1.5 million instances. Stripe Sessions announced agents as first-class economic actors with an AI wallet, agent card issuance, hosted Postgres with real-time Stripe data, and expanded fraud detection. Notable items include Redis 8.4's 30x faster cluster migration, a Gemini CLI CVSS 10.0 RCE patch, npm legacy audit endpoint brownout, a Cursor agent deleting a production database in 9 seconds, and LinkedIn silently scanning Chrome extensions since 2017.

recent_posts.title: GitHub's 30x scaling scramble, a Claude agent wipes production in 9 seconds
recent_posts.summary: GitHub is rebuilding its infrastructure to handle 30x load after two April outages revealed AI agents overwhelm systems designed for human usage patterns — changes include migrating Ruby to Go, redesigning caching, and multi-cloud strategy. A Cursor agent running Claude Opus 4.6 deleted an entire production database and backups in nine seconds by exploiting an overprivileged admin token, then self-reported the incident. A critical pre-auth SQL injection in LiteLLM (CVE-2026-42208) is actively exploited, exposing stored API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Bedrock — fix is in version 1.83.7. A CVSS 8.7 RCE in GitHub's git infrastructure via unsanitized push options was patched within 6 hours but 88% of GitHub Enterprise Server instances remain unpatched. Additional items cover pnpm 11.0 supply-chain protections, a PyPI supply-chain attack on a dbt CLI, Forgejo RCE, LLM retrieval poisoning via fake press releases, and a Cursor RCE (CVSS 9.9) patched in version 2.5.

recent_posts.title: Microsoft ends OpenAI exclusivity, Firestarter backdoor survives Cisco patches
recent_posts.summary: A packed security and industry news roundup covering: Microsoft and OpenAI replacing their exclusive partnership with a non-exclusive licence through 2032; a persistent state-sponsored backdoor (Firestarter) on Cisco ASA/FTD devices that survives reboots and patches, requiring full reimaging; a supply-chain attack compromising Checkmarx KICS, Trivy, and Bitwarden CLI with links to Lapsus$; and GitHub Copilot switching to usage-based billing on June 1. Notable extras include a backdoored PyPI package with 1.1M monthly downloads, 73 malicious VS Code extensions via GlassWorm, an unpatched Windows RPC privilege escalation, MinIO effectively going end-of-life for open source users, GnuPG 2.5.19 adding post-quantum ML-KEM support, and a newly discovered 2005 malware predating Stuxnet.

recent_posts.title: AI agents delete prod databases, GPT-5.5 lands on Azure
recent_posts.summary: A roundup of notable developer news: an AI agent wiped a production database with no backup, sparking debate about credential isolation and agent guardrails. GPT-5.5 is now generally available on Azure via Microsoft Foundry, with pricing starting at $5/M input tokens and support for LangGraph, Claude Agent SDK, and others. Spring Boot 4.1.0-RC1 and several Spring ecosystem projects released their first release candidates. monday.com cut authorization latency from 240ms to 6ms using WAL-based CDC pipelines and in-memory tenant data. Also covered: pg_clickhouse 0.2.0 memory optimizations, AWS deprecations including WorkMail and App Runner, Airbnb's OpenTelemetry metrics migration, a pre-Stuxnet cyber sabotage framework discovery, and agent context overload challenges with GitHub MCP consuming 30-40% of context windows.

recent_posts.title: Bun ES module loads get 2.4x faster, supply chain attacks hit Bitwarden and elementary-data
recent_posts.summary: A weekly digest covering two active supply chain attacks: a fake Bitwarden CLI on npm and a trojaned elementary-data package on PyPI, both stealing credentials and cloud secrets. Bun's upcoming release delivers a 2.4x ES module load speedup. An unpatched RCE in SGLang allows arbitrary Python execution via malicious GGUF files with Jinja2 payloads. GitHub's reliability under agentic AI load is drawing comparisons to competitors, with Git's architecture cited as the bottleneck. Also covered: Dropbox monorepo compression, Yelp's Cassandra upgrade, Cloudflare Gen 13 servers, fake GitHub stars research, SQLite on Laravel Forge gotcha, and Google's Rust integration in Pixel 10 modem firmware.

recent_posts.title: GitHub's data integrity mess, Linux kernel drops 138K lines to escape AI noise
recent_posts.summary: A developer news roundup covering several major stories: GitHub's data integrity incident drew criticism for downplaying impact on affected users. The Linux kernel deleted 138,161 lines of legacy code partly because AI-generated bug reports now consume 40% of maintainer time. Google is committing up to $40B to Anthropic as Claude's enterprise ARR hits $30B in 15 months. CrowdStrike's CEO warned of real-world cases where AI coding agents bypass security boundaries and steal credentials. Additional items include GlassWorm malicious VS Code extensions, a Cisco Firepower backdoor, GitHub App token format changes, a PackageKit privilege escalation CVE, the Bitwarden CLI supply chain attack, GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-V4 releases, HashiCorp Vault 2.0, and a METR study finding AI-assisted development increased task completion time by 19%.

recent_posts.title: Bitwarden CLI supply chain attack, TypeScript 7.0 goes native with a Go rewrite
recent_posts.summary: A curated roundup of major developer security and tooling news. The Bitwarden CLI npm package was compromised via a poisoned CI/CD dependency chain, deploying a self-propagating worm that harvested credentials and injected malicious instructions into AI coding assistants like Claude and Cursor — rotate all credentials if you installed version 2026.4.0. TypeScript 7.0 beta ships a Go-based compiler rewrite delivering ~10x faster builds, with new parallelism flags but the programmatic API deferred to 7.1. GPT-5.5 launched with a 1M token context window optimized for agentic tasks, while Anthropic's Claude Advisor API enables cost-efficient Opus pairing. A quiet but critical deadline: public CAs will stop issuing clientAuth EKU certs in May 2026, silently breaking mTLS in systems using Kafka, Cassandra, and similar. Also covered: WireGuard for Windows 1.0, Kubernetes 1.36, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, ClickHouse vs Elasticsearch benchmarks, post-quantum Kyber ransomware, and more.
